svg.text: Interface connector (one per signal group; arrow = active to passive)

The enclosing frame is the parent module; blocks inside are its instances and functional groups (FG = functional group of the module own logic). [pulse] = one-cycle signal, [level] = held value. Interface labels outside the frame mark connections to the outside.
Top level of a CAN protocol controller for microcontroller-style hosts. It joins the host bus to an internal register file, a bit-timing generator and a frame-processing engine, and exposes the s
HOST, RX, TX, BOS, IRQ, CKO, CLK
Register file seen by the host. It stores the operating mode (basic or extended), command requests, interrupt enables, bit-timing parameters, the error-warning limit, the acceptance code and mask
HRA, RRD, CSI, BTI, IRQ, CLK, CKO
Bit-timing generator. It derives the time quantum from the programmed prescaler, divides every bit into a synchronization segment, a first phase segment (including the propagation segment) and a
Frame-processing engine. On reception it decodes identifier, control, data, CRC, acknowledge and end-of-frame fields with bit de-stuffing and CRC checking, filters accepted identifiers with an ac
FAC, FRI, CSI, BSI, CLK, BOS, TX
Converts the multiplexed host bus into single-clock accesses. It captures the address presented on the shared lines while the address-latch strobe is active, detects the active edge of the write
Read-path multiplexer. From the latched address and the operating mode it decides whether a host read targets the received-message window or an ordinary register, selects the corresponding data s
Receive-line synchronizer. It passes the asynchronous CAN receive input through two flip-flops clocked by the core clock to remove metastability before the bit-timing generator uses it, and is in
